report.004: ## How to read this report (for players)
report.005: It is fine if the technical details below look confusing. Just hand this whole file to any AI and let it adjust your mod order based on the conclusions in section 1.
report.006: In one sentence: this playset has %d cases of mods overwriting each other, of which %d **cannot be fixed by reordering the load order** and %d can be solved by reordering. Another %d are mods overwriting vanilla, which is normal.
report.007: "Mods overwriting each other" means two mods claim the same content and only one can win. For the ones where reordering the load order is no use, the winner is already decided by the file name, so dragging the mod to the bottom of the list will not save it.

report.015: These mods sit below the other one in the playset, so they should have won, but they did not win because their file name loses in filename order. To make one win you must rename the file or make a compatibility patch.
report.018: ### 1.2 Subscribed a mod but nothing changed: the mod lost to vanilla (%d)
report.019: Vanilla is always loaded first and has the lowest priority, but a mod does not necessarily win the filename comparison. This is the most typical case of "subscribed but see no change".
report.020: - [%s] `%s`: winner is vanilla (`%s`), the mod's file is %s
report.021: ## 2. Assumptions behind the verdicts (must read before analysis)
report.022: Stellaris decides in this order: **first by filename ASCII order, and only when the file names are identical does it look at the load order in the launcher**.
report.023: So there are two kinds of conflicts, and they are handled completely differently:
report.024: - **Reordering works**: the conflicting files have exactly the same name (same path, whole-file replacement). Just put the mod you want to win below the other one.
report.025: - **Reordering does not work**: the conflicting file names differ. The winner is decided by filename ASCII order, **changing the load order has no effect at all**, and you can only rename the file or make a compatibility patch.
report.026: Vanilla joins the comparison first in the load order and with the lowest priority, so a mod does not necessarily win.
report.027: The overwrite semantics table comes from the official wiki's Common folder list plus local testing. After a major game update the rules for some folders may change. If you doubt a winner given in this report, trust what is actually recorded in error.log: search for `already exists, using the one at`, and the file named on that line is the one that really takes effect.
